label: input token z during the original phase
explanation: Token detector for the letter z when it is read as an original token (before <DEL>). Fires on every original-phase z step (precision 1.0 on dev) and on no other input token. Strongest when z is the first token (t=0, ~1.0 of max); activation falls as z appears later in the sequence (often ~0.5-0.7 of max at t=6-8), and a repeated z is somewhat weaker than the first. Does NOT fire on the delimiter, and almost never on z fed back in the copy phase: only 537 copy-phase steps with tiny activations (~0.05-0.1 of max, mostly recall_idx 1 when the sequence began with z), holding ~0% of the mass.

issues: Test split matches the reported scores: precision 1.0, recall 0.995, F1 0.998, mass recall 0.9996, with 0 false positives.

The 505 missed test steps are all copy-phase steps where z is fed back at recall_idx 1, in sequences that start with z. Their activations are 0.00-0.08 of max and they hold 0.0% of the mass. This matches the explanation and is not a meaningful gap.

Minor: the magnitude falls off with position a bit more steeply than the explanation says. Estimated from mass share per active step, the mean activation relative to t=0 is about 0.57 at t=6, 0.46 at t=7 and 0.38 at t=8, not the stated 0.5-0.7. The qualitative claim (strongest at t=0, weakening later in the sequence) holds.
The delimiter never activates the feature (0 active steps), and only the input token z ever activates it (all of the mass is on z).
